answer: Every attestation path through the graph is capped by a min-cut: no cluster of identities can push more endorsement than the narrowest bottleneck separating it from the rest of the network. A sybil cluster hiding behind one lantern account must dig a fresh grove of independent paths to any other cluster, since bundling more edges into the same plume of connections only saturates the existing bottleneck rather than opening a new one. Because min-cut capacity never sums across colluding clones, every extra identity costs a full set of fresh, disjoint edges, not a shared fee.
